slice_id: intraday P19 EquityReplay refuses a buy entry it cannot afford

phase0_history.design: EquityReplay tracks its own running Decimal cash balance, updated in _queue_fill from every fill (both kinds, both sides); _process_entries refuses a side=="buy" entry whose cost exceeds it, gated by the existing self._cash_flow_composer is not None check from ADR-0176
phase0_history.review: fresh independent design skeptic, cold review, independently verified every code claim (account-ignored, fee-computed-after-open_lot, TICK_PHASES ordering, HorizonBook.open_lot's no-mutation-on-refusal, the PaperAccounting/shadow-rung pin, the Decimal(str(x)) idiom's consistency with _proposal_for, the ADR-0176 gate's non-interaction with existing tests, the halt-queue retry path's absence of a double-_queue_fill risk): 0 Critical, 0 Major, 3 Minor, GO. All three Minors fixed in place before RED: a wrong citation (Decision point 4 quoted CLAUDE.md prose that does not exist -- it is a pinning test's name, test_nodes_capital.py:698) and two Required Phase-0 matrix rows made explicit (the short-entry test is genuinely new coverage, not an extension of exercised behavior; the override-then-refused-for-insufficient-cash sequencing is deliberately tested as accepted pre-existing behavior)

phase0_history.design: adds Decision point 1.5 -- _submit_due_cash_flows also credits self._cash_balance by the sum of each due cash-flow record's amount, inside the existing if due: block, right after append_many
phase0_history.reason: self-found during RED/build by the opus builder, before any implementation landed: it wrote the required Phase-0 matrix tests first per TDD and correctly refused to go further when 3 of them could not pass against Revision 1's own Decision text -- Revision 1 tracked the balance from fills only, so the ADR-0176 cash-flow deposits reaching the ledger never reached the balance this ADR gates buys against, meaning every buy would refuse forever whenever a cash_flow_policy was configured. Genuine gap in the approved design, not a builder error.
phase0_history.verdict: accepted without a second fresh Phase-0 round -- the one-line addition reuses the exact Decimal-sum idiom already present and already Phase-0-reviewed in ADR-0176's own _submit_due_cash_flows for the identical purpose, introducing no new architecture, so this revision proceeded directly to the two mandatory final review lenses

reuse_confirmed.method: dedicated pre-drafting sweep via a background read-only Explore agent, covering dskit/production/guards.py, breaker.py, encumbrance.py, leg.py, loop.py, and EquityReplay's own propose/evaluate/queue pipeline in full
reuse_confirmed.findings: the toolkit's one existing cash-sufficiency mechanism (encumbrance.SettledFundsShortfall + a Limit guard + EncumberedAccounting) is opt-in and structurally unreachable for this replay -- the shadow/paper rung it declares pins accounting to the paper kind by name (dskit/production/compose.py's _simulated() rung table), under which PaperAccounting.snapshot always sets available == total, so nothing reduces available cash regardless of document edits. EquityReplay.proposals receives the tick's AccountState but never reads it. Nothing else in the replay path checks cash sufficiency at all -- confirmed total, not partial, before drafting a from-scratch child-owned mechanism instead

non_authority: This slice adds a refusal (not a new authority) entirely within EquityReplay's own child-owned bookkeeping. No dskit/production module changed. No new capability, registry entry, or uses: site. No margin/short-collateral modeling, no partial fills or automatic position-size scaling (a refused buy is refused outright, in full, never resized), no interaction with turnover/cost policy beyond reusing the existing unchanged per-share fee formulas, no ReplayRun/P4 wiring, no change to ADR-0176's own cash-flow-policy/composer code. No backtest launch, no paper/live trading, no deployment.
